mutants.name: extracted files not compared by size
mutants.explanation: The next branch of the same else-if chain compares the SHA-256 of the extracted file. Two byte strings of different length cannot have the same SHA-256 (collision resistance), so a size difference is always reported by the hash branch. The verdict (ok false) is identical for every input; only the wording of the problem changes. The earlier layer (entry size from the zip table against the inventory) also reports it.
mutants.demonstration: proofs/archive-demo.json: five honest tamper cases and three simulated extractor failures (extra file, skipped file, truncated file); the M03 verdict equals the original verdict in all eight.

mutants.name: extra extracted files tolerated
mutants.explanation: Every file the standard reader (System.IO.Compression ExtractToDirectory) writes corresponds to an entry of the zip table, and the entry loop already reports any entry that is not in the inventory. The guard can only fire if the extractor writes a file that has no entry. Residual: under a simulated misbehaving extractor that plants an extra file the mutant accepts the archive (verdict differs); no input that the standard reader produces reaches this difference. No executable change was made. This is a disclosed non-material residual for S25-A02.
mutants.demonstration: proofs/archive-demo.json: honest reader cases identical; simulated extra file: original false, M04 true.

mutants.name: unextracted files tolerated
mutants.explanation: With the guard disabled the else-if chain dereferences found.bytes on an undefined value, which throws a TypeError that the surrounding catch converts into a problem. mutants.name: marker may be non-comment text
mutants.explanation: Not equivalent. Without the comment requirement a marker in non-comment text becomes the anchor: (a) an earlier mention of the marker hides the real comment that follows (alertCaseBound true becomes false), and (b) a marker trailing the interval line itself anchors a block that has no comment above it (false becomes true). Neither was tested. New tests cover both.
